pretest.title: Start with your current understanding
pretest.introduction: Answer using your current understanding. No answer feedback is provided during the session.

fields.prompt: Before this session, how familiar were you with carbon accumulation models?

options.label: I have heard of them but have not studied the models
I have used or built such a model

fields.prompt: The water already inside a tank is…
Inflow decreases from 10 to 6 L/min. Outflow stays at 4 L/min. After this change, the amount of water in the tank…
A tank contains 30 L. Inflow and outflow are both 5 L/min. How many litres are in the tank after 10 minutes?
Explain your answer about the change in the amount of water when inflow decreases.

posttest.title: Revisit your understanding
posttest.introduction: Use what you have learned. No score or answer feedback is shown on this page.

fields.prompt: In the waste case, which quantity is a stock?

options.label: Tonnes of waste processed per day
Tonnes of waste waiting at the storage site
Tonnes of waste arriving per day

fields.prompt: Water is already present in a storage area. Runoff is 40 m³/min and drainage capacity is 60 m³/min. While water remains available, the amount of stored water…
There are 45 tonnes of waste. Incoming waste and processing are both 7 tonnes/day. How many tonnes remain after 3 days?
Why does reducing inflow not necessarily reduce the amount already accumulated?

transfer.title: Apply your understanding in a new context
transfer.introduction: Consider a simplified, clearly bounded CO₂ reservoir. Emissions add CO₂ and uptake removes it. Assume a constant uptake rate and a nonnegative stock. Ignore other processes. This is an educational model, not a real atmospheric forecast.

fields.prompt: Which quantity is a stock in this reservoir?

options.label: The amount of CO₂ in the reservoir

fields.prompt: Emissions decrease from 12 to 8 tonnes of CO₂/year. Uptake stays at 6 tonnes of CO₂/year. After emissions decrease, the amount of CO₂…
The reservoir contains 100 tonnes of CO₂. Emissions stay at 8 and uptake stays at 6 tonnes of CO₂/year. How many tonnes of CO₂ are in the reservoir after 5 years?
While stock remains available, which condition makes the amount of CO₂ decrease?

options.label: Emissions decrease but remain higher than uptake

fields.prompt: Explain the relationship between emissions, uptake, and the change in the amount of CO₂. What condition must a policy achieve to reduce the stock?
